items.t: Prologis stock: Company breaks ground on Georgia warehouse
sum: Prologis broke ground on a new speculative distribution facility at its Prologis 75 Commerce Center in Jackson, Georgia, according to Bisnow in a report published Thursday, November 12. The project adds capacity to Prologis' industrial platform as leasing activity in the Metro Atlanta market remains elevated.

The speculative building will cover 1.29 million square feet. Prologis said the facility is intended to meet demand for modern, well-located distribution space while giving customers flexibility and access to major transport routes.

Bisnow reported that Prologis operates more than 20 million square feet of distribution space in Georgia. The new building will feature roof spans of up to 42 feet, a specification designed to support users with taller-clearance requirements.

CBRE data cited by Bisnow showed 6.7 million square feet of net absorption in the Metro Atlanta industrial market during the third quarter, while leasing activity reached a record 22.2 million square feet. Demand was led by third-party logistics, automotive supply chains and infrastructure-related users.

For investors, the project offers another development opportunity in a market with strong tenant activity. Returns will depend on construction execution, leasing progress and the capital required to bring the facility into operation.

Is Prologis (NYSE:PLD) Nearing Its SEGRO Deal?
sum: - The warehouse landlord is moving its agreed takeover of Britain's SEGRO toward completion.
- The tie-up would sharply widen the group's European logistics footprint and development pipeline.
- A fresh supply-chain study flags power access and fast delivery as the forces reshaping where goods flow.

The recommended combination, struck earlier in the year and now working its way through the approvals that stand between announcement and close, would hand the enlarged group a dramatically wider spread of sheds, land, and development projects across the continent. Under the agreed terms, owners of SEGRO stock would receive newly minted Prologis shares, with a partial cash alternative on the table for those who prefer cash in hand. The customer is also pursuing a secondary London listing as part of the plan. Prologis (NYSE:PLD) Real Estate Prologis Inc (NYSE:PLD) 130.11 USD -0.445 0.341% Last Updated at: 2026-11-10T21:00:00Z is part of the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and NYSE Composite.

The scale on the table is striking. The reach extends to raw land and projects still on the drawing board. For a business whose value rests on owning the right sheds in the right places, that expanded canvas is the heart of the rationale.

Europe sits at the center of the logic. The continent's dense cities, tangled borders, and uneven warehouse supply make well-placed distribution space scarce and prized, and e-commerce keeps stoking demand for sheds close to where people live. By deepening its European presence, the group ties itself more tightly to the structural march of online retail and the reshaping of supply chains across the region. The move also rides the broader wave of nearshoring and regionalizing that has swept global trade. As companies pull production and inventory closer to end markets to steady their networks, demand for modern warehouses near major population centers climbs.

At its foundation, the company is the world's largest owner and operator of logistics real estate. It builds, owns, and leases the vast distribution centers and warehouses that form the physical spine of modern commerce, renting space to retailers, parcel carriers, manufacturers, and the e-commerce giants that move goods from shelf to doorstep.

Fibra Prologis stock trims outlook as occupancy eases
sum: FIBRA Prologis reported third-quarter 2026 results on October 21, highlighting resilient industrial-property operations in Mexico while narrowing parts of its full-year outlook. The company said period-end occupancy was 96.5 percent and average occupancy was 95.1 percent.

The FIBRA Prologis earnings release said customer retention was 66.0 percent and same-store cash net operating income increased 1.7 percent. Net effective rents on lease renewals rose 36.2 percent, while the company started leases covering 2.9 million square feet.

Net earnings per CBFI reached US$0.1095, compared with US$0.0530 in the third quarter of 2025. FFO per CBFI was US$0.0574, up from US$0.0561 a year earlier. The figures show stronger earnings per certificate, although occupancy and customer retention were lower than in the prior-year quarter.

For 2026, management guided to FFO of US$0.2400 to US$0.2500 per CBFI, excluding the impact of the incentive fee. Year-end occupancy is expected at 96.5 percent to 97.5 percent, while same-store cash NOI growth is projected at 7.0 percent to 8.0 percent. Building acquisitions are planned at US$100 million.

As of September 30, FIBRA Prologis had leverage of 24.2 percent and approximately US$1.2 billion of liquidity. That liquidity included US$1.0 billion of available capacity under its unsecured credit facility and US$167 million of unrestricted cash.

FIBRA Prologis is a Mexican real estate investment trust that acquires, owns and manages Class-A industrial properties in Mexico. According to the company's company profile, its portfolio covers six geographic markets and focuses on high-quality industrial buildings serving logistics and manufacturing demand.

In its earnings release, the Mexican industrial real estate trust said net effective rents on rollover rose 36.2 percent and funds from operations per CBFI reached 0.0574 dollars.

Period-end occupancy was 96.5 percent, compared with 98.0 percent in the third quarter of 2025. Average occupancy stood at 95.1 percent, while customer retention declined to 66.0 percent from 81.7 percent.

Leases commenced during the quarter covered 2.9 million square feet, down from 4.1 million square feet a year earlier. Same-store cash net operating income rose 1.7 percent, compared with 14.8 percent in the prior-year quarter.

FIBRA Prologis set its 2026 year-end occupancy outlook at 96.5 to 97.5 percent and its same-store cash NOI growth forecast at 7.0 to 8.0 percent. The trust also set building acquisitions at 100 million dollars and maintained its full-year distribution guidance at 0.1700 dollars per CBFI.

As of September 30, leverage was 24.2 percent and liquidity was approximately 1.2 billion dollars, including 1.0 billion dollars of available unsecured credit capacity and 167 million dollars of unrestricted cash. Management said improving customer demand and lower construction starts were encouraging signs, while the portfolio's rent mark-to-market offered potential support as market conditions improve.

FIBRA Prologis owns and operates Class-A industrial real estate in Mexico, with logistics and manufacturing facilities across six core markets. items.t: Prologis Inc. stock gains as investors digest $19 billion SEGRO deal and valuation debate
sum: Prologis Inc. stock (ISIN US74340W1036) is trading around USD 135 on the New York Stock Exchange as of September 11, 2026, leaving investors to weigh the impact of the company’s planned USD 19 billion acquisition of UK warehouse operator SEGRO and the resulting valuation debate.

According to Simply Wall St on September 11, 2026, Prologis has agreed a USD 19 billion transaction to acquire SEGRO, significantly expanding its European logistics footprint and data-center exposure.

As AINvest reports, Prologis funded part of the cash consideration by issuing roughly 15 million new shares in a public offering that raised about USD 2.1 billion at an offer price of USD 140 per share, with the stock closing that day down about 2.8 percent at the offering level.

The same analysis notes that, at about USD 134 per share, Prologis is trading near 22 times the midpoint of this year’s core funds-from-operations (FFO) guidance, implying a premium valuation relative to some industrial real estate peers and highlighting how much future growth from the SEGRO and data-center strategy is already priced in.AINvest

In its September 11, 2026 note, Simply Wall St estimates a fair value of about USD 128 per Prologis share, which it states is roughly 5.2 percent below the recent market price, implying that the stock could be modestly overvalued following the SEGRO announcement.

The implied comparison is clear: if investors accept a fair value of USD 128 while the shares change hands near USD 135, the premium is around USD 7 per share, or a bit more than 5 percent, suggesting that expectations for future rental growth and development returns are elevated.

For investors, the key question now is whether incremental earnings from SEGRO’s portfolio and a pivot toward data-center assets will be sufficient to grow core FFO enough to justify paying roughly 22 times the midpoint of this year’s guidance, as highlighted by AINvest.

sum: Prologis Inc agrees to acquire SEGRO plc in a £14.0 billion deal, expanding its European footprint by 47% and creating a combined portfolio of 368 million square feet. The transaction offers SEGRO shareholders 0.0920 new Prologis shares per share, with a partial cash alternative capped at £3.5 billion.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

Prologis Inc has agreed to acquire UK-based logistics real estate company SEGRO plc in a recommended transaction valued at approximately £14.0 billion. Announced on Aug. 4, 2026, the deal marks a significant expansion of Prologis' European platform, combining the two companies' portfolios into a global entity with approximately £200 billion of assets under management. The acquisition strengthens Prologis' position in the European logistics market, creating an operating portfolio of 368 million square feet and expanding its European footprint by 47%. For shareholders, the move aims to enhance long-term earnings potential while maintaining credit ratings.

The transaction structure involves SEGRO shareholders receiving 0.0920 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share held. Shareholders may elect to receive cash in lieu of some or all of their Prologis share consideration under a partial cash alternative. The maximum aggregate amount of cash available under this alternative is approximately £3,509,777,110.70. Each shareholder's basic entitlement under the partial cash alternative equals 25% of the fixed price of 1,031.7 pence per SEGRO share, translating to 258 pence in cash and 0.0690 new Prologis shares for each SEGRO share if only the basic entitlement is elected. Elections exceeding the basic entitlement will be scaled back pro rata if total requests exceed the maximum cash amount.

SEGRO shareholders will also be entitled to receive and retain any 2026 interim dividend of up to 10.14 pence per share and any 2026 final dividend of up to 22.56 pence per share, which SEGRO intends to pay prior to closing. The cash consideration payable under the partial cash alternative will be funded through a committed term loan facility entered into on Aug. 4, 2026, existing liquidity, and other available sources of funding.

items.t: Prologis Strikes Deal to Acquire Segro in £14.3 Billion Logistics Property Merger
sum: Prologis (NYSE:PLD) has reached an agreement to acquire Segro Plc (LSE:SGRO) in a transaction worth approximately £14.3 billion, combining two of the world's largest industrial property owners. Once completed, the enlarged business will oversee around $269 billion of logistics real estate assets, significantly increasing Prologis' scale across Europe.

The agreed offer values Segro at 1,031.7 pence per share, with investors receiving 0.0920 newly issued Prologis shares for each Segro share they own. The offer represents a 14.4% premium to Segro's most recently reported net asset value of 902 pence per share.
Including the proposed 2026 final dividend of up to 22.56 pence per share, the overall value rises to 1,054.3 pence per share.

As an alternative, shareholders may elect to receive part of their consideration in cash. Up to £3.5 billion has been allocated for the cash option, representing one quarter of the total transaction value. Those selecting the standard mixed consideration will receive 258 pence in cash alongside 0.0690 Prologis shares for each Segro share held. If requests exceed the available cash pool, allocations will be reduced proportionally. Prologis said the cash component will be financed through committed borrowing facilities and existing cash resources.

The acquisition will substantially strengthen Prologis' position in Europe by adding Segro's extensive warehouse portfolio. Together, the combined group will manage approximately 368 million square feet of logistics space across the continent.

The merger will also expand Prologis' European development pipeline to around 13 million square feet while more than doubling its regional land bank, providing significant capacity for future projects.

"This deal brings together SEGRO's exceptional portfolio and customer relationships with Prologis' global platform, operating expertise and financial strength," Prologis Chief Executive Daniel S. Letter said.

Following submission of our latest proposal, senior representatives of Prologis, Inc. ("Prologis") met with SEGRO plc ("SEGRO") management in London on Sunday. Having submitted a revised proposal only days earlier, the purpose of that meeting was not to present a further revised offer, but rather to understand whether there was a credible path to a transaction capable of recommendation by the SEGRO Board.
We were disappointed that the discussion did not provide meaningful clarity regarding the matters that would enable further progress.

Prologis' assessment of SEGRO's value is grounded in the quality of its real estate and our expectations for its long-term performance. The NAV reflects SEGRO's independent valuers' assessment of the value of all development land and property assets owned by SEGRO as at 30 June 2026. It is very unusual for a real estate defence document to publish a declining NAV during an offer period.

sum: Prologis PLD is slated to report its second-quarter 2026 results on July 16, before the opening bell. In anticipation of the announcement, industry analysts and investors are eager to assess the company's performance and prospects in the current economic climate.

In the last reported quarter, this leading industrial REIT posted core funds from operations (FFO) per share of $1.50, up 5.6% from a year ago. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 1.49%. Results were supported by robust leasing activity.

Over the trailing four quarters, Prologis beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate for FFO per share on three occasions and met in the remaining period, with the average beat being 2.09%. This is depicted in the graph below:

The U.S. industrial real estate market strengthened further in the second quarter of 2026. According to a Cushman & Wakefield report, national vacancy declined to 6.9%, suggesting the market has moved beyond its cyclical peak. Net absorption increased 21% from the prior quarter to 62.1 million square feet, bringing first-half demand to 113.6 million square feet — the strongest first-half performance since 2023.

Occupiers continue to favor buildings with higher clear heights, stronger power capacity and infrastructure suited for automation and AI systems. Dallas–Fort Worth, Phoenix, Atlanta and several Midwest logistics hubs performed well, while port markets, including Houston, New Jersey, Los Angeles and Savannah, GA, also posted healthy demand.

Leasing activity accelerated despite longer transaction timelines. Year-to-date leasing reached a four-year high, up 16% from a year earlier, with Dallas–Fort Worth, the Inland Empire and Chicago leading the country. Third-party logistics companies and manufacturers accounted for more than 55% of leasing volume as businesses expanded and adjusted their supply chains.

Supply remained relatively controlled. Second-quarter deliveries totaled 62 million square feet, down 16% year over year, while first-half completions were 19.2% below the same period in 2025. At the same time, the construction pipeline increased to 305.1 million square feet, up 18% from a year earlier. More than one-third of the pipeline is build-to-suit, reducing the risk of excessive speculative supply.

items.t: Prologis Reveals Rejected $16.6B Bid for Segro; UK Logistics REIT Shares Surge
sum: Industrial real estate giant Prologis (NYSE: PLD) disclosed Wednesday that it made an unsolicited £12.6 billion ($16.6 billion) all-stock proposal to acquire UK-based logistics property owner Segro Plc (OTC: SEGXF), a bid that was swiftly rejected by Segro’s board.

Under the proposed terms, Segro shareholders would have received a 24.6% premium to the company’s closing share price and would have owned approximately 10.5% of the combined entity. Despite the rejection, Segro shares surged as much as 16% in London trading following the disclosure.

Prologis said a combination of the two companies would create a stronger global logistics platform, citing the complementary nature of their European warehouse portfolios and opportunities to expand development projects and data center initiatives. The company also pointed to its lower leverage profile, greater access to capital and history of delivering superior shareholder returns as key advantages of a merger. According to Prologis, the transaction could unlock meaningful cost savings and revenue synergies through operational integration.

The San Francisco-based REIT is the world’s largest owner of logistics real estate, with approximately 1.3 billion square feet of warehouses, distribution centers and industrial facilities across major markets in North America, Europe, Asia and Latin America. The company serves many of the world’s largest retailers, manufacturers and e-commerce operators, making it a critical player in global supply chains.

Financially, Prologis remains one of the strongest companies in the industrial REIT sector. The company generated more than $8 billion in revenue in 2025 and reported core funds from operations of roughly $5.70 per share. Its investment-grade balance sheet, substantial liquidity and relatively low leverage have supported continued expansion through development projects, acquisitions and growing investments in data center infrastructure.
Segro’s board, however, rejected the proposal “immediately and unequivocally,” signaling little interest in pursuing discussions at this stage.

Wall Street Analysts Think Prologis (PLD) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
sum: When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?
Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Prologis (PLD).

Prologis currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.92, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 24 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.92 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.
Of the 24 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 13 are Strong Buy, representing 54.2% of all recommendations.

The ABR suggests buying Prologis, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Do you wonder why? As a result of the vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover, their analysts tend to rate it with a strong positive bias. According to our research, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations for every "Strong Sell" recommendation.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

Why Kevin Warsh's Debut Could Surprise - & 2 Stocks Stand to Gain
On Wednesday, Kevin Warsh will step to a podium inside the Federal Reserve's headquarters and take questions as Fed Chair for the first time.

Sworn in on May 22nd after a 54-45 Senate vote, Warsh will have just gaveled out his first FOMC meeting, and the rate decision itself is a foregone conclusion — the committee is universally expected to hold the federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75%, where it has sat since December. Nearly 100% of futures traders expect no change.
So the decision isn't the story. The tone is — and I think there's a real chance Warsh sounds more dovish than the hawkish consensus expects.

Here's the conventional wiring of this meeting. Inflation has run hot this year — the April reading hit a three-year high — and the energy spike from the Iran war made it worse. The widespread expectation is that the updated Summary of Economic Projections will skew hawkish, showing both higher inflation and a slightly higher path for rates.
On paper: a hawkish hold, a higher-for-longer dot plot, and a new chair with a reputation for inflation vigilance.

items.t: Two Josh Brown stocks bucking the real estate headwinds: The new data center landlord and a mall owner
sum: (This is The Best Stocks in the Market , brought to you by Josh Brown and Sean Russo of Ritholtz Wealth Management.) Josh — I'm old enough to remember when people were bullish on Prologis (PLD) because of its reputation as "the landlord of e-commerce" circa 2021. I was trading the stock back then for this exact reason. When Amazon and every other retailer needed warehouse space close to consumers, Prologis had the locations, the scale, and the relationships. That story hasn't gone away, but there's a new one running alongside it. The company is now pushing aggressively into data centers, using both conversions of existing warehouses and greenfield developments, with publicly stated ambitions to scale data center capacity to as much as 10 gigawatts over the next decade. Corporate customers tied to U.S. data center construction are making up an increasing share of Prologis's forward-looking pipeline, as suppliers move their distribution centers closer to data center developments. The world's largest industrial REIT is quietly becoming a digital infrastructure company, and most investors still have it filed under "e-commerce warehouses." The benefit of doing our Best Stocks in the Market research is that it forces me to ask why a stock in the "wrong" sector might be among the market's leaders when most people just hear the name and ticker and revert back to their previously held biases. "Oh, Prologis, that's that ecommerce REIT I used to hear about during Covid." Guess again, fat boy. New era, new fundamental driver. Sean's going to explain to you why Prologis and another REIT everyone thinks they understand, Simon Property Group (SPG) , are acting well this year despite everyone's concerns over higher interest rates - a well understood negative catalyst for most of the sector. items.t: Prologis Sees Greater Focus on Supply Chain Adaptability in 2026
sum: Melinda McLaughlin, global head of research at Prologis, Inc. (NYSE: PLD), joined the REIT Report to review major supply chain trends expected for 2026.

McLaughlin discussed the performance of international logistics markets, the impact of e-commerce on leasing demand, the growing power needs of logistics facilities, emerging trends in defense-related demand, and the challenges faced by the trucking industry.

The conversation highlighted the need for adaptability in supply chains as companies navigate a changing landscape. “I think there's an acknowledgement that supply chains need to be adaptable rather than continue to wait for perfect information. And I think that's really going to shape a return to normal in a lot of different spheres of the logistics real estate market,” McLaughlin said.
- A more “normal” balance is emerging for logistics demand between inland and coastal hubs.
- Prologis expects international logistics markets to outperform in 2026.
- Europe is experiencing tightness in logistics markets due to structural factors.
- Brazil is seeing historical lows in vacancy rates, leading to fast rent growth.

Prologis (PLD) Q4 2025 Earnings Call Transcript
Prologis sees record lease signings in 2025
sum: Logistics warehouse operator Prologis signed a record number of new leases in 2025 as more customers are going long on real estate coming out of a prolonged downturn and trade war scare.

Prologis (NYSE: PLD) reported fourth-quarter consolidated revenue of $2.09 billion on Wednesday, up 8% year over year and in line with analysts’ expectations. Core funds from operations (FFO) of $1.44 per share also matched the consensus estimate.

“2025 was a record year for lease signings, setting the business up with strong momentum for 2026,” said Prologis CEO Dan Letter in a news release. “Customers are making long-term decisions with greater conviction, and we are meeting that demand with a platform that brings logistics, digital infrastructure and energy together at a global scale.”

The San Francisco-based real estate investment trust inked deals representing 228 million square feet of space last year even as on-again, off-again tariffs crimped customer demand. The industry was also dealing with a post-Covid hangover as new property deliveries were met with sagging demand.

New leases commenced in the fourth quarter were down 6% y/y to 43.8 million square feet. Average occupancy fell 30 basis points y/y to 95.3%. However, that was the highest occupancy rate of the year and a sign that the market has likely bottomed. (Occupancy was 95.8% to close the quarter.)

The company’s 2026 guidance calls for core FFO of $6.00 to $6.20 per share, which brackets the consensus estimate of $6.13. The guide assumes average occupancy in a range of 94.75% to 95.75% and development starts between $3 billion and $4 billion.
Shares of PLD were up 1.6% in premarket trading on Wednesday.
